segments: and the care of the kingdom,
and he would not reply.
Then he relented and wrote to him and addressed him
"lawful king,
and refuge of the Muslims,
Rukn al-Din Sultan Toghril Beg,"
and entreated him on behalf of the people of Isfahan,
and sent it with an envoy.
And Toghril Beg, as he was waiting for this,
accepted his supplication,
and sent in return for these things
twenty thousand dinars to the treasury of the Caliph al-Qaim,
and two thousand dinars to the administrators of the kingdom.
And from here Sultan Toghril Beg began to draw the shape of a bow at the top of a document,
and within it these titles.
And that mark was called
the "Tughra";
and he who drew it when commanded [was called]
the "Tughrai".
And in the year 449
[449] (443?) of the Arabs,
an envoy came from Constantine, the King of the Romans, to the Caliph al-Qaim of Baghdad,
and with him a letter in Greek,
and between its lines its translation in Arabic,
in letters of gold upon purple parchment, thus:
"Constantine, faithful, exalted, mighty king in Christ God,
sole Augustus in the kingdom of the Romans,
Monomachos,
to the beloved friend,
the honored Abu Jafar al-Qaim,
head of the Muslims,
and Commander of the Faithful,"
and the rest of the other words of love.
And in the year 446
[446] of the Arabs,
when all the countries of the Persians were subjugated under the dominion of Sultan Rukn al-Din Toghril Beg,
he set his face toward the lands of the Romans.
And he went against the fortress of Manzikert,
and sat against it for a long time,
and was not able to conquer it,
and plundered the country.
And he also came and plundered the country of Arzun al-Rum (Erzurum), which belonged to the Romans until then,
and turned back to spend the winter in Azerbaijan,
so that he might return again {OCR?} to the land of the Romans.
And in the year 1365 [of the Greeks],
[1365] in Later Kanun (January),
Constantine, the King of the Romans, the husband of Queen Theodora, passed away.
And she governed for one year.
And she sent an envoy to Baghdad to the Caliph,
and confirmed the peace by means of the tribute that she took upon herself.
And in that year Sultan Rukn al-Din Toghril Beg sent an envoy to the Caliph and said:
"I desire to come and be honored in the service of the Prophet."
